who: developer running 2-3 AI coding agents on one repo
pain: Parallel agent sessions on the same repo overwrite and revert each other's files and cause merge conflicts
workaround: separate git worktrees, one tmux session per agent, short task note per worktree

who: developer running an implementing session and a reviewing session in parallel
pain: Two sessions share one working tree so uncommitted edits collide and a branch switch in one breaks the other, leaving unintended repo states

who: developer with about ten repos and two or three active AI sessions at once
pain: Three parallel sessions each rewrote the same shared config file whole and none could see the others; a rule in the instruction file did not prevent it
workaround: hooks and a mailbox file for cross-project requests

who: developer running 3-4 coding agents on different features of one repo
pain: Coordination overhead and conflicts when several agents work concurrently on the same repository
workaround: built a personal git worktree orchestrator

who: Claude Code users opening several terminals against one repo
pain: Recurring weekly questions on stopping parallel sessions from clobbering the same file and what multi-agent instructions should say
workaround: hand-written rules, file locks and scratch directories

who: Claude Code user working across several sessions
pain: Context must be carried between sessions and compaction slows work, so shared state has to be kept by hand
workaround: keep a plan.md and other shared context files, compact early, resume after limits

who: developer building a large project who keeps hitting Claude limits
pain: Needs a way to turn a project into a phased plan with todo lists so agents stay focused and work can move between tools
workaround: write a spec in markdown, split it into many tiny tasks, have agents pick tasks one at a time

who: developers asking how to plan and structure AI-built projects
pain: Large builds and migrations risk lost functionality unless a written plan is the source of truth and work is split into verified tasks
workaround: plan documents, built-in plan modes, section-by-section breakdown handed to agents

who: developer splitting a build into task files for several agents
pain: Wants a repeatable structure of spec file plus per-task files that any agent can pick up

who: developers sharing how they document AI-built projects
pain: Single PLAN and agent-instruction docs stopped being enough as projects grew
workaround: separate plan and agent instruction files, then planning tools

pain: Wants reusable guardrail, skill and template files so repeatable project standards do not clutter the context
workaround: guidelines file, settings guardrails, skills with bundled template files

who: Claude Code users setting up several agents
pain: Do not know what the instruction file should contain when multiple agents run at once
